newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ACCC to carefully examine Westpac deal.
newsitem.headline: ACCC to carefully examine Westpac deal.

text.p: Anti-monopolies authority, the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC), said on Thursday that it would carefully examine the proposed merger between Westpac Banking Corp and Bank of Melbourne Ltd.

"The ACCC's approach to all mergers is to examine each case individually on its merits, taking into account the nature of the transaction and the circumstances prevailing at the time," ACCC chairman Allan Fels said in a statement.
"The ACCC's approach to mergers is to conduct enquiries in the marketplace about their likely effect. These enquiries typically take several weeks to conclude," Fels said.
Fels said subsmission from Westpac and the Bank of Melbourne are expected in the next week.
Westpac proposed friendly offer values the Victorian-based bank at A$1.435 billion.
The merger must be approved by Treasurer Peter Costello and the ACCC, who have said in the past they would not approve mergers that removed the last regional bank from a state market.
Bank of Melbourne is the last significant regional bank in Victoria, but the merger plan is for the two banks to merge the retail operations in Victoria and keep the Bank of Melbourne name.
Westpac's offer values each bank of Melbourne share at A$9.75.
